advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix docs/plan-review-gate.md:53-55: a bug is NOT subject to the not-claimable fast-fail (claimability._REVIEWED_TYPES excludes bug); it short-circuits past the fast-fail and proceeds to the bug-tier advisory review.
evidence: docs/plan-review-gate.md:53-55: "a `bug` is reviewed under the bug tier (see above) and so is subject to this fast-fail like any other reviewed type."
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py:62-63: `if ticket_type not in _REVIEWED_TYPES:` / `return None` — a bug short-circuits, no fast-fail

src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py:14-16: docstring: 'Only the gate-reviewed graph types (task/story/epic) are guarded — bug/session_log short-circuit to an exempt PASS with no LLM cost, so refusing them would save nothing.'
The bug review tier (workflow_ops.py:170-185) runs the DET floor + necessity probe but is a distinct mechanism from the claimability fast-fail; being reviewed does not entail being fast-failed.
advisory.finding: The not-claimable fast-fail subsection now asserts a `bug` 'is subject to this fast-fail like any other reviewed type,' but the fast-fail (claimability.not_claimable_verdict) is scoped to _REVIEWED_TYPES = ("task", "story", "epic") and returns None for a bug, so a bug is NOT subject to it.
scenarios: A reader relies on the doc to reason about whether `review-plan` on a not-yet-claimable bug will fast-fail (INDETERMINATE) versus proceed to the bug-tier advisory review — the code does the latter, the doc now says the former.
advisory.suggested_fix: Rephrase to: '`session_log` / `code_review` / `identity` tickets are exempt from the whole gate and unaffected; a `bug` is also not subject to this claimability fast-fail — it short-circuits past it (claimability only guards task/story/epic) and proceeds to its light advisory bug-tier review.'
